I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best, it fits my well irrigation, and after 30 years I trust it for steady grain and lower risk. I will put `8.0 mu` into winter wheat and then follow it with summer maize on the same `8.0 mu`. I will keep `2.9 mu` in cotton because it still gives me cash income, but I will not expand it because cotton takes more labor and pest control, and some people in my family work off-farm. I will use better seed on all three crops because I want more stable emergence and yield. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level, not too low because I have irrigation and want output, and not too high because that wastes money. For wheat I will irrigate twice and manage for a stable, medium-high yield. For maize I will use no-tillage after wheat harvest to save time and labor, then give one irrigation if needed from the well. For cotton I will manage more carefully with more potassium, more irrigation, and more pesticide sprays because that crop is more sensitive and more labor-heavy. Overall, I will run the farm in a practical way: steady grain from wheat and maize, some cash from cotton, and labor-saving choices where possible.
